infra_notes.retail: Wire every checkout lane — reliability beats everything. 1–2 APs cover staff + guest.
infra_notes.restaurant: KDS and printers get WIRES (kitchens are Wi-Fi-hostile). Tableside terminals on a dedicated staff SSID.
infra_notes.qsr: Minimal: 1–2 APs, a few drops. Kiosks want wired Ethernet, not Wi-Fi.
infra_notes.hotel: The big one — an AP every 4–8 rooms, PMS on its own VLAN, more switches per floor. Cost scales with rooms, not revenue.
infra_notes.grocery: Large footprint = more APs (3–6). Every lane wired; size the PoE switch for cameras too.
infra_notes.salon: Minimal — 1 AP, 2–3 drops. The booking PC holds card-on-file data: segment it.

options.label: Quote-based — varies by mount type
options.note: Mount HARDWARE is retail (e.g. POS wall mount ~£33.60 ex VAT, printdesigns.com); install LABOR is the quote part — no published per-device install-labor price found. Ask your local POS installer.

install.name: Cable drops — per run
install.sub: Pulled by a low-voltage contractor — one-time, paid at install, never monthly. Building asset: outlives the POS by 10–20+ yrs.

options.label: US$150–250 per Cat6 drop — midpoint US$200
options.note: US$150–250 commercial per drop (datawiresolutions.com); US$175–285 tested/certified (Rx Technology); harder Cat6A/plenum/after-hours runs US$200–350+. USD — plus exchange. Same work as Infrastructure → Network cable drops above — use one, not both.

options.label: Quote-based — varies by site
options.note: New build with open ceilings is cheap; retrofit through finished walls costs more. Get per-run pricing.

options.label: Quote-based — per site
options.note: No standalone published price — usually bundled with the install. Context: full Wi-Fi install US$2,500–15,000+ depending on coverage; general IT labor US$75–200/hr as proxy (thenetworkinstallers.com). Config survives hardware refresh if documented.

options.label: US$500–1,500 professional install — midpoint US$1,000
options.note: US$500–1,500 professional POS installation per location (theposexchange.com); US$200–1,000 one-time setup/onboarding (swyftpos.com); Toast-era US$300–500. USD — plus exchange. Industry benchmark: US$1,000–5,000 total hidden implementation on top of hardware + software quotes.

options.label: Quote-based — per location
options.note: Taxes, tenders, receipts, users and permissions. Bigger catalog = more hours.

options.label: Quote-based — per location
options.note: No standalone published price — usually bundled with implementation (Toast onboarding does menu build; Rezku includes one-on-one training + custom menu build). A 20-item café menu is an afternoon; a 10,000-SKU grocery catalog is a project.
